title: The Pacific
hook: Island battles and command geography across a vast ocean.
notes: Original Orbis factual annotations checked 14 October 2026; event-card links and scene-indexed notes identify the evidence. Points locate selected places approximately, not military fronts, camp boundaries or casualty-density surfaces. Contemporary coastlines are reference geography; modern country borders are hidden unless a scene explicitly compares country status. No comprehensive monthly occupation map is claimed. Sources by scene: 1. Pearl Harbor brings the United States into the war: https://www.nps.gov/wwii/learn/historyculture/pearl-harbor.htm; 2. Midway: a battle around an atoll: https://www.history.navy.mil/content/history/museums/nmusn/explore/photography/wwii/wwii-pacific/turning-the-japanese-tide/1942-june-battle-of-midway.html; 3. Guadalcanal opens a southern campaign: https://www.history.navy.mil/research/library/online-reading-room/title-list-alphabetically/b/battle-of-guadalcanal.html; 4. Command areas crossed the date line: https://maps.lib.utexas.edu/maps/historical/history_ww2.html; 5. Okinawa: fighting close to Japan: https://www.history.navy.mil/content/history/museums/nmusn/explore/photography/wwii/wwii-pacific/okinawa.html Army atlas source/title/date and credit: https://maps.lib.utexas.edu/maps/historical/history_ww2.html. Pacific boundaries divide Allied command areas, not Japanese occupation. Original scan used without a geographic warp; provisional wide-area polynomial fit was rejected as too inaccurate. Map anchors are rounded locations from the scan’s named geography.

scenes.title: Pearl Harbor brings the United States into the war
scenes.text: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941. The harbour in Hawaii was a major US naval base; the attack brought the United States into World War II. Hawaii was then a US territory, not yet a state.

scenes.title: Midway: a battle around an atoll
scenes.text: The June 1942 battle near Midway checked Japanese expansion in the central Pacific. The Navy identifies the main carrier battle on 4 June; the point locates the atoll rather than reconstructing fleets’ positions.

scenes.title: Guadalcanal opens a southern campaign
scenes.text: US Marines landed on Guadalcanal on 7 August 1942. The campaign combined land, sea and air fighting around the Solomon Islands. The point locates the island’s northern shore, not a landing beach perimeter.

scenes.title: Command areas crossed the date line
scenes.text: The Army’s map of 1 August 1942 divides Allied commands across the Pacific. It shows why Hawaii and Australia mattered as distant organising centres. These printed boundaries classify commands, not land occupied by Japan; the original scan is shown below.

media.alt: US Army atlas map titled The Pacific Areas, 1 August 1942, showing Allied command boundaries across the ocean.
media.caption: Command areas, 1 August 1942; not Japanese occupation. Original unwarped scan.

scenes.title: Okinawa: fighting close to Japan
scenes.text: US forces landed on Okinawa’s main island on 1 April 1945. The battle brought devastating combat to its civilian population as well as Japanese and Allied forces. No casualty estimate or occupation perimeter is inferred from this point.
